title: Embedding variant splitter: progressive rollout, SLA-aware routing, and deprecation timeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We are onboarding two new embedding variants (embed-v2-small and embed-v2-latency) that improve reranker quality for short queries and reduce tail latency for 99th percentile respectively. Both variants require coordinated changes across the embed gateway, routing rules, and the reranking endpoint to allow canaries, traffic splits, and graceful deprecation of older 1.x variants.

Goals: 1) Provide a safe progressive rollout mechanism that can split traffic by tenant and request shape (short vs long queries). 2) Ensure SLA-aware routing so latency-sensitive tenants prefer the low-tail variant while cost-sensitive tenants default to the smaller model. 3) Define a clear deprecation schedule and automated fallback for model versions reaching end-of-life. 4) Add telemetry and alerting to detect quality regressions (embedding similarity drift) and latency regressions per tenant.

Scope: This ticket covers the embedding gateway changes (routing policy + variant splitter), reranking endpoint adaptation (accepts model_version header and falls back safely), rollout orchestration (canary, A/B by tenant), telemetry dashboards and SLO checks, and the deprecation automation (notifications, tenant pinning, sunset job).

Design decisions and trade-offs: - We considered doing a global weighted rollout only, but that doesn't let us target tenant-specific SLAs. We'll implement a two-level splitter: tenant affinity rules + global weights. - To avoid increased cold-starts on embed pools, the gateway will allocate a minimal warm pool for new variant traffic during canaries. This increases short-term cost but keeps tail latency bounded. - For similarity regressions detection, we will use a combination of holdout prompt sets (per tenant where available) and embedding distribution drift metrics (cosine distribution shifts). This is more complex than simple regression checks but catches silent quality changes.

Implementation plan: 1) Gateway: add variant_splitter service that evaluates routing policies (tenant metadata, request length, cost tier) and emits routing decisions_into request headers. 2) Reranker: accept X-Embed-Variant header, validate compatibility, and fallback to pinned version if new variant unavailable. 3) Rollout API: expose admin endpoints (console + API) to create canary groups, set weights, and pin tenants. 4) Telemetry: instrument per-variant latency histograms, embedding norm distributions, and evaluate a per-tenant quality score computed from holdout similarity lists. 5) Deprecation: create a deprecation-runbook generator that notifies tenant owners, suggests pinning, and schedules auto-sunset if no response.

Acceptance criteria: - Edge-case tests: reranker falls back to pinned variant within 100ms on failure. - Load tests: system supports progressive canary where 5% of traffic uses new variant without increasing 99th percentile latency by more than 10% for latency-sensitive tenants. - Telemetry: dashboards for per-variant latency, cost, and quality drift are available. - Rollout UI: Console allows creating a tenant-targeted canary and shows estimated cost delta. - Deprecation automation: system can schedule and send a sunset notice and perform auto-migration pin if tenant is unresponsive after 30 days.

Telemetry and validation: We'll onboard two synthetic holdout sets: general-web-short (n=5k pairs) and enterprise-search-long (n=2k pairs). Quality checks run nightly and compute embeddings cosine similarity deltas and AUC on reranker test harness. Alerts trigger on >3% drop in holdout similarity or >10% increase in 99th percentile latency for a tenant.

Persistence and compatibility: Model_version will be expressed as semantic strings (e.g., v2-latency-202603) and recorded in request logs and tracing spans. We will maintain a minimal compatibility matrix (stored as a small YAML in config repo) to prevent pairing untested reranker/model combinations.

Rollout timeline: Week 1: Gateway variant_splitter and basic routing rules (dev + unit tests). Week 2: Reranker header support + canary API. Week 3: Small internal canary (platform team), telemetry dashboards. Week 4: Gradual tenant canaries and deprecation-runbook automation. Week 6: Full rollout for low-risk tenants and start sunset of selected 1.x variants.
